names: P11 -- landscaped median strip connecting Mission Bay Circle to P11A
summary: A tree-lined median strip running within the road right-of-way, connecting the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout east to the P11A half-circle island; a real, already-landscaped median per satellite imagery, hand-traced with the property owner's guidance and fit to a rotated rectangle. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P11/11A' together among the parcels already managed by SF Recreation and Parks (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

milestones.text: Already part of RPD's managed open-space inventory as 'P11/11A' (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this median was built, not its actual construction date

sources.title: Mission Bay Parks Open Space (CAC Item 2, September 2023)
sources.publisher: Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (sfocii.org)

sources.title: Mission Bay Commons Parks (P12, P13, P15); Active Recreation Parks (P7, P9) -- Mission Bay Future Parks (CAC Update, November 14, 2024)
sources.publisher: Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (sfocii.org)

open_questions: No public source names this specific median strip or gives its own construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already RPD-managed by that date (grouped with P11A), which is an upper bound, not a build date.

A separate, later OCII source (the Nov 2024 CAC deck, src-ocii-openspace-2024) instead groups the label 'P11' together with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 under the still-interim 'Mission Bay Commons' area near 3rd Street and Mission Bay Boulevard -- a different location from this record's median strip near Mission Bay Circle. This repo's own digitization_method log already describes correcting an earlier session's own wrong location guess for P11 (made from that same source note) after the property owner pointed to this median strip instead; the underlying conflict between the two OCII documents' own use of 'P11' is not resolved here, only flagged.
Owner/operator beyond 'part of RPD's Mission Bay open-space inventory' not confirmed by any source found.
